title: A Schoolboy's Ice Cream Showed Hot Water Can Freeze Faster

scenes.text: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water. Physicists still argue about why.
In 1963, a Tanzanian schoolboy named Erasto Mpemba put hot ice cream mix in the freezer.
It froze before his classmates' cooled mix. His teacher laughed at him.
Years later he tested it with a physicist, and they published it in 1969. It's now called the Mpemba effect.
In 2020, scientists in Canada made a tiny hot system cool faster than a warm one, again and again.
Evaporation, dissolved gases, frost, nobody agrees which matters most. A student's ice cream still beats the experts.

description:
The Mpemba effect: under some conditions, hot water can freeze faster than cooler water. Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba noticed it with ice cream mix in 1963 and published it with physicist Denis Osborne in 1969.
In 2020, Simon Fraser University researchers reported the effect in a controlled microscopic system (Nature). Whether and why it happens in ordinary water is still debated.
Have you ever tried it?
